content:
Unit 5 - Passage Structure — Title & Goal
Learn to master unit 5 - passage structure questions for the Digital SAT through a short concept, a modeled item, and targeted practice.

Key skill

Read the note and focus on what the question is really asking inside the passage.

  • Locate explicit claims and implicit ideas.
  • Ask: What is the passage mainly doing?
  • Match answers to the most general accurate statement.

Model item

Study how the evidence in the passage supports the correct answer.

Passage — The article first describes a problem with shoreline erosion, then outlines a pilot project that slows wave impact.

Question 1. Which choice best describes the passage’s structure?

  • Cause-and-effect
  • Chronological narrative
  • Comparison of two theories
  • Definition followed by example
Problem then solution → A (cause leading to effect).

Quick practice

Try these quickly. Eliminate two choices before choosing your answer.

Passage — Paragraph 1 introduces a study; Paragraph 2 presents results; Paragraph 3 discusses implications.

Question 2. Which sentence would best begin Paragraph 3 to improve cohesion?

  • Another study used a different method.
  • These findings suggest a practical application in coastal planning.
  • Participants enjoyed the study.
  • Coasts vary around the world.

Next skill

Build on the previous skill. Compare how this question type reads the passage differently.

Note: Locate the exact phrase or sentence that proves your choice.

Another model item

Notice how small wording differences change the best answer.

Passage — The author contrasts two proposals and ultimately recommends the second.

Question 3. Which choice best describes the organization?

  • Problem–solution
  • Comparison–evaluation
  • Anecdote–analysis
  • Process description

More practice

Aim for accuracy first, then speed. Re-check the evidence that rules out each wrong choice.

Passage — The instructions list steps to assemble a device.

Question 4. Which transition would best signal sequence?

  • Meanwhile,
  • Afterward,
  • Nevertheless,
  • In contrast,

Mixed practice set

These mix multiple skills. Mark the question type before you start, then solve.

Passage — The editorial explains that although Proposal X cuts costs, Proposal Y better protects services.

Question 5. Which structure best fits the passage?

  • Cause–effect
  • Sequence
  • Compare–contrast
  • Definition
